topic: What interference mitigation techniques are viable for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations?
consensus_response: The high polarization correlation coefficients (0.4-0.5) of small-scale fading components at Tx lead to increased cochannel interference in overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations. To mitigate this, Rate Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) can be employed to enable simultaneous transmission with reduced co-channel interference. Additionally, Analog Beamforming (ABF) can adaptively steer the beam to optimize signal reception and minimize multipath interference. Cognitive Radio techniques can also complement RSMA and ABF by adaptively adjusting transmission parameters based on channel conditions and user demands.
